segments.say: Let's go somewhere peaceful now, just for a little while. There's nothing to learn here and nothing to do. Just a quiet place to rest. Imagine a small wooden cabin, standing on its own near the edge of a calm sea. It's late evening, and the last of the light is fading over the water.

Inside, the cabin is simple and warm. There's a small stove, glowing softly, and the gentle crackle of a wood fire. A soft bed sits by the window, piled with blankets. The floorboards are smooth and warm under your feet. Everything here is slow and quiet, and nothing is asking anything of you.

Through the window, you can see the sea. It's very calm tonight. Small waves roll in slowly, one after another, and spread out across the sand with a soft hush, before drawing back again. In, and out. Just like your breath.

show.cap: A cabin by a calm sea

segments.say: Imagine lying down on the soft bed by the window. Pull the blankets up around your shoulders. They're heavy and warm, like a gentle hug. Your head sinks into the pillow. The fire crackles quietly across the room. And outside, the sea goes on breathing, slow and steady.

Let your breath fall into rhythm with the waves. As a wave rolls in, breathe in, slowly. As it draws back across the sand, breathe out, even more slowly. In, with the wave. And out, with the water sliding back. There's no need to count. The sea will keep the time for you.

A wave rolls in, and you breathe in. It spreads across the sand. It draws back, and you breathe out. And then a little pause, a soft silence, before the next one comes. Again, and again, all through the night.

show.title: Breathing with the waves
items: A wave rolls in, breathe in
A pause, before the next one

segments.say: Now, if you like, we'll count slowly down from ten to one. With each number, let yourself sink a little deeper into the bed, a little further into rest. You don't need to do anything except listen, and let the numbers carry you down.

Ten. Your whole body is heavy and warm. Nine. Your shoulders drop a little lower. Eight. Your breath is slow, like the waves outside. Let each number be like a step down a soft staircase, leading somewhere quiet and safe.

Seven. Your arms and legs are sinking into the blankets. Six. Your face is soft, your jaw is loose. Five. You're halfway down now, and the sounds of the room are growing faint and far away, like voices heard from another room in a big, quiet house.

Four. There's nothing you need to hold on to. Three. The fire is a soft glow, the sea a gentle hush. Two. Your thoughts are slowing, softening, drifting apart like mist over water. One. And here you are. Deep, warm and still. Completely at rest.

show.title: Four, three, two, one
items: A soft glow, a gentle hush

segments.say: Stay here for a while, at the bottom of the soft staircase, deep in your rest. There's nothing to do here. Nowhere to be. No one to become. Just the warmth of the blankets, the glow of the fire, and the slow sound of the sea.

If a thought comes to you, that's alright. Imagine placing it gently on a small wave, and watching it drift slowly out to sea. Further and further, smaller and smaller, until it's just a tiny point of light on the dark water, and then it's gone. The sea will hold it for you until morning.

show.sub: Let it drift out to sea

segments.say: The tide comes in and goes out, twice every day, every day of the year. It never hurries. It never stops. It doesn't worry about whether it's doing it right. And over long years, it slowly shapes the whole coastline, smoothing rocks and building beaches, one gentle wave at a time.

Change can be like that too. Gentle. Patient. Never in a hurry. Slowly shaping everything it touches. You don't need to force it. You only need to keep coming back, like the tide, day after day, and let time do the rest.

The stove glows a little lower now. Its warmth spreads slowly across the cabin, into the blankets, into your hands and feet, into the very centre of you. You're warm all the way through. Warm, and heavy, and calm.

Perhaps, now, a soft rain begins to fall on the cabin roof. Very gentle. A light patter on the wooden shingles, steady and soothing. It makes the cabin feel even warmer, even safer. You're snug inside, and the rain can't reach you. It can only sing you towards sleep.

Listen to the rain and the sea together. The patter above. The hush of the waves below. Two soft sounds, weaving together into one slow lullaby. You don't have to do anything at all. Just lie here and listen, and let the sound fill the space where your thoughts used to be.

On the window, small drops of rain gather and run slowly down the glass, catching the faint glow of the fire. One drop joins another, and another, making little rivers that wind their way down. Watch them, if you like, or simply let your eyes close.

You are safe here. Held by the warm cabin, by the soft bed, by the steady sea and the gentle rain. The night is long and kind. It will keep you until morning, and you don't need to do anything to deserve it. Rest is simply yours.

You may feel yourself drifting further now, the edges of everything becoming soft and blurred. The cabin, the fire, the rain, the sea, all melting together into one warm, quiet feeling. Let it happen. There's nothing to hold on to, and nothing to lose.

We're almost at the end of our journey together tonight. Just one last stretch of quiet, and then the long, deep rest of the night. Stay as you are. Warm, heavy and still. Let the sea keep breathing for you.
